usage: Used to describe something that is fresh, especially food, flowers, or plants that still look lively and not dried out.
Very common before nouns in plant and food descriptions, like 鮮花, 鮮葉, or 鮮果.
Can sound a bit literary or old-fashioned on its own; in everyday speech people often use it in set phrases or more specific words.
For learners: 鮮重点 is on freshness and liveliness, not just ‘newly made’.
